question: With which of the following rights do Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution deal with?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right Against Exploitation**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Right Against Exploitation:**

 
 
• Articles 23 and 24 of the Indian Constitution specifically deal with the Right Against Exploitation.
 
• Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labor.
 
• Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 in any hazardous occupation.
 
• These articles aim to protect vulnerable individuals from exploitation and ensure their dignity.
 
• These articles are fundamental rights, and are enforceable by the supreme court of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Freedom of Religion:**

 
 
• The Right to Freedom of Religion is guaranteed by Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These articles provide for the freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• They also ensure the freedom to manage religious affairs and the freedom from taxation for promotion of any particular religion.
 
• These rights are designed to protect the secular nature of India.
 
• These rights allow people to practice any religion that they choose.
 
 
 
• **Right to Equality:**
 
 
• The Right to Equality is guaranteed by Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These articles provide for equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination, equality of opportunity in matters of public employment, abolition of untouchability, and abolition of titles.
 
• These rights are aimed at ensuring social justice and equality for all citizens. 
 
• These rights are fundamental to the Indian constitution.
 
• These rights are designed to remove social inequalities.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies:**
 
 
• The Right to Constitutional Remedies is guaranteed by Article 32 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article empowers citizens to move the Supreme Court to seek remedies for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• It is considered the "heart and soul" of the Indian Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• It provides for the issuance of writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto.
 
• This right allows people to go to the supreme court, to ensure their rights are upheld.
 
• This right is a very important part of the Indian legal system.
